findings.issue: The truthiness check treats max_price=0 as if no limit were supplied.
findings.evidence: R1 says zero means only free products; T1 says, "if limit" return matching products, otherwise return all items.
findings.failure_scenario: A request with max_price=0 returns products with positive prices.
findings.fix: Check whether limit is missing (None), rather than whether it is truthy.

findings.issue: Filtering happens after pagination, so the plan does not filter the entire catalog before paginating.
findings.evidence: R2 requires filter, sort, THEN paginate; T2 calls paginate(rows, offset, size) before filter(page, max_price).
findings.failure_scenario: If a page contains expensive products while matching products fall on later pages, the response omits those matches and may be underfilled.
findings.fix: Filter all tenant rows by max_price, sort the filtered rows by immutable product ID, then paginate.

findings.issue: The proposed tests do not exercise the zero-price case or a page boundary, so they can miss both implementation defects.
findings.evidence: T3 lists missing limit and limit=1500 but not limit=0; its test data is "all within a single page."
findings.failure_scenario: The endpoint tests can pass while max_price=0 returns paid products and pagination omits matching products beyond the current page.
findings.fix: Add a zero-limit test and a multi-page case with matching products beyond the first page.
